common.disclaimerText: NutriSense is a rule-based nutritional awareness portal. It maps self-reported dietary habits and symptoms to general nutrition science benchmarks. It does NOT medically diagnose nutritional deficiencies, prescribe therapeutic doses, or replace blood tests (e.g. Ferritin, Vitamin D, or B12 panels). If you experience persistent symptoms, consult a qualified physician or registered dietitian.
common.disclaimerCompact: Preliminary nutritional risk indication only — not a clinical medical diagnosis.
common.disclaimerSubtleText: NutriSense provides dietary habit analysis and preliminary risk indications. All recommendations are derived from ICMR-NIN 2024 guidelines and do not replace laboratory testing or professional medical advice.

footer.description: A Smart Nutritional Deficiency Detection and Awareness Portal. Helping individuals evaluate dietary habits, understand micronutrient synergy, and identify possible risk patterns based on evidence-backed nutritional benchmarks.
footer.rdaBenchmark: Mapped to 2024 Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDA) for Indians.
footer.localArchDesc: Built using Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts. All rule evaluation executes locally in your browser with zero external server or database tracking.
footer.zeroCloudDesc: Assessment data is retained only in your browser's localStorage.
footer.healthNoticeDesc: NutriSense is a nutritional awareness platform. It provides general dietary insights and preliminary risk indications based on user-entered answers. It does NOT constitute medical diagnosis, clinical advice, or a substitute for laboratory testing. Always consult a qualified physician or registered dietitian for medical evaluation.

sedentary.label: Sedentary
sedentary.desc: Mostly sitting during the day with little or no regular exercise (such as a desk job).

lightly_active.label: Lightly Active
lightly_active.desc: Light daily movement or walking 1 to 3 days a week.

moderately_active.label: Moderately Active
moderately_active.desc: Moderate exercise, sports, or brisk walking 3 to 5 days a week.

very_active.label: Very Active / Heavy Work
very_active.desc: Heavy daily exercise, sports training, or physically demanding work.

vegetarian.label: Vegetarian (Lacto-Vegetarian)
vegetarian.desc: Plant foods and dairy (milk, curd, paneer). No eggs, meat, or fish.

ovo_vegetarian.label: Ovo-Vegetarian
ovo_vegetarian.desc: Plant foods and eggs. No dairy, meat, or fish.

vegan.label: Vegan
vegan.desc: Only plant foods. No dairy, eggs, meat, or animal products.

pescatarian.label: Pescatarian
pescatarian.desc: Plant foods, dairy, eggs, and fish or seafood. No meat or poultry.

non_vegetarian.label: Non-Vegetarian
non_vegetarian.desc: All food types, including meat, poultry, fish, eggs, and dairy.

step2.title: Step 2: Food Group Consumption Frequency
step2.subtitle: How frequently do you consume each of these 9 key Indian food categories?

fruits.title: Fruits
fruits.question: How often do you eat fruits?
fruits.subtitle: Fresh whole fruits in your regular meals or snacks.
fruits.examples: Apples, bananas, papaya, oranges, guava, and amla.

vegetables.title: Other Vegetables
vegetables.question: How often do you eat other vegetables (besides leafy greens)?
vegetables.subtitle: Cooked or raw vegetables consumed throughout the week.
vegetables.examples: Carrots, tomatoes, gourds, pumpkin, cauliflower, and capsicum.

greenLeafy.title: Green Leafy Vegetables
greenLeafy.question: How often do you eat green leafy vegetables?
greenLeafy.subtitle: Cooked greens, saag, or leafy additions to dals and curries.
greenLeafy.examples: Palak (spinach), methi, drumstick (moringa) leaves, amaranth, and sarson.

pulsesLegumes.title: Dal, Beans & Pulses
pulsesLegumes.question: How often do you eat dal, beans, or lentils?
pulsesLegumes.subtitle: Lentil soups, whole pulses, and legume dishes.
pulsesLegumes.examples: Toor dal, moong dal, chickpeas (chana), rajma, and sprouted beans.

dairyOrAlternatives.title: Milk & Dairy Alternatives
dairyOrAlternatives.question: How often do you have milk, curd, or dairy alternatives?
dairyOrAlternatives.subtitle: Dairy products or fortified plant-based milk drinks.
dairyOrAlternatives.examples: Milk, curd (dahi), paneer, buttermilk (chaas), or fortified soy/almond milk.

eggsMeatFish.title: Eggs, Meat & Fish
eggsMeatFish.question: How often do you eat eggs, poultry, meat, or fish?
eggsMeatFish.subtitle: Animal-source foods (automatically marked as Never for vegetarian/vegan diets).
eggsMeatFish.examples: Eggs, chicken, fish, mutton, or other seafood.

nutsSeeds.title: Nuts & Seeds
nutsSeeds.question: How often do you eat nuts or seeds?
nutsSeeds.subtitle: Nuts, dry fruits, and edible seeds eaten raw or added to meals.
nutsSeeds.examples: Almonds, walnuts, peanuts, sesame seeds (til), and chia or flaxseeds.

wholeGrainsMillets.title: Whole Grains & Millets
wholeGrainsMillets.question: How often do you eat whole grains or traditional millets?
wholeGrainsMillets.subtitle: Whole grain rotis, millets, and unrefined grains.
wholeGrainsMillets.examples: Ragi, bajra, jowar, whole wheat roti, brown rice, or oats.

fortifiedFoods.title: Fortified Foods
fortifiedFoods.question: How often do you consume fortified foods?
fortifiedFoods.subtitle: Common packaged staples enriched with essential vitamins and minerals.
fortifiedFoods.examples: Double fortified salt (iron + iodine), and packaged milk or oil with added vitamins.

step3.title: Step 3: Self-Reported Indicators & Lifestyle Factors
step3.subtitle: Common symptoms and daily lifestyle habits that influence nutrient absorption.

frequentFatigue.title: Do you often feel tired or low on energy?
frequentFatigue.subtitle: Feeling drained or lacking energy during normal daily activities.

generalWeakness.title: Do you often feel physically weak or get tired easily?
generalWeakness.subtitle: Lack of physical muscle strength or tiring quickly during ordinary tasks.

difficultyConcentrating.title: Do you often have trouble concentrating or remembering things?
difficultyConcentrating.subtitle: Mental fatigue, difficulty staying focused, or occasional memory lapses.

paleAppearance.title: Have you noticed unusual paleness or brittle nails?
paleAppearance.subtitle: Unusually pale skin, pale inner eyelids, or easily broken nails.

muscleCrampsWeakness.title: Do you often experience muscle cramps or bone discomfort?
muscleCrampsWeakness.subtitle: Frequent calf cramps, muscle spasms, or dull body and joint aches.

hairSkinChanges.title: Have you noticed unusual hair loss or dry skin?
hairSkinChanges.subtitle: Noticeable hair shedding, dry or rough skin patches, or slow healing of small cuts.

poorAppetite.title: Do you often have a poor appetite or changes in your sense of taste?
poorAppetite.subtitle: Reduced desire to eat or noticeable changes in how food tastes.

sunExposure.title: How much time do you usually spend outdoors in daylight?
sunExposure.subtitle: Sunlight exposure helps your body naturally produce Vitamin D.

adequate_daily.label: Daily (20+ minutes)
adequate_daily.desc: Regular time spent outdoors in daylight on most days.

moderate_weekly.label: A few times a week
moderate_weekly.desc: Some time outdoors or occasional daylight exposure.

teaCoffeeWithMeals.title: How often do you drink tea or coffee with or immediately after meals?
teaCoffeeWithMeals.subtitle: Drinking tea or coffee close to meals can reduce how well your body absorbs iron from food.

often.label: Often or daily with meals
often.desc: Regularly drink tea or coffee during or right after meals.

sometimes.label: Sometimes
sometimes.desc: A few times a week with meals.

rarely.label: Rarely or never
rarely.desc: Usually keep a gap of an hour or more from meals.

sleepQuality.title: How many hours do you usually sleep each night?
sleepQuality.subtitle: Adequate rest supports daily energy and overall recovery.

guidelines.title: Nutrition Guidelines & Methodology
guidelines.subtitle: Explore the scientific references, rule-based inference models, Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDA), and evidence-based methodology powering the NutriSense portal.
guidelines.sectionADesc: NutriSense references established public health standards published by premier Indian and international health authorities.
guidelines.sectionsBCDesc: How user inputs are structured and matched against nutritional criteria.
guidelines.collectDemoDesc: Age, biological sex, height, weight (BMI calculation), and physical activity level.
guidelines.collectDietDesc: Vegetarian (lacto), vegan, non-vegetarian, ovo-vegetarian, or pescatarian habits.
guidelines.collectFoodDesc: Frequency of consuming fruits, vegetables, green leafy vegetables, pulses, dairy/alternatives, animal proteins, nuts/seeds, whole grains, and fortified items.
guidelines.collectLifestyleDesc: Energy levels, skin/hair texture, muscle cramps, direct sunlight exposure, and mealtime tea/coffee habits.
guidelines.considerBioDesc: Distinguishes between plant-based (non-heme) and animal-based (heme) micronutrients, accounting for absorption enhancers and inhibitors.
guidelines.considerInhibitorDesc: Accounts for tannins in mealtime tea/coffee which suppress plant iron absorption by up to 60–80%.
guidelines.considerSexDesc: Applies elevated iron requirements for biological women (29 mg vs 19 mg per ICMR).
guidelines.considerSynthesisDesc: Considers sunlight duration for Vitamin D and dietary fats for fat-soluble vitamins (A & D).
guidelines.sectionDDesc: A step-by-step visual representation of how user input transforms into explainable nutritional recommendations.
guidelines.rdaTableDesc: Daily nutrient targets for reference Indian adults used as evaluation baselines in NutriSense.
guidelines.sectionEDesc: Essential boundaries regarding system capabilities and medical non-diagnostic framing.

workflow.step1Desc: Collects age, biological sex, anthropometrics (BMI calculation), physical activity level, and dietary preference (vegetarian, vegan, non-veg).
workflow.step2Desc: Evaluates weekly consumption frequencies across 9 crucial food groups against ICMR-NIN recommended dietary frequencies.
workflow.step3Desc: Screens for self-reported physical sensations (fatigue, cramps, skin changes) alongside lifestyle factors (sunlight, tea habits).
workflow.step4Desc: Cross-evaluates dietary intake deficits against reported indicator weights using transparent, rule-based scoring algorithms.
workflow.step5Desc: Generates non-diagnostic risk levels (Low, Moderate, Elevated) with human-readable rationale and ICMR-aligned whole-food recommendations.

limitations.lim1Desc: NutriSense is an educational nutritional awareness platform developed to foster dietary awareness. It does NOT provide clinical diagnoses or replace professional laboratory blood work (such as serum ferritin, 25-OH Vitamin D, or serum B12 tests).
limitations.lim2Desc: Assessment accuracy is directly contingent upon the completeness and fidelity of user-entered answers regarding food frequency and physical indicators.
limitations.lim3Desc: Individual nutrient absorption is governed by genetics, gastrointestinal health, prescription medications, microbiome diversity, and underlying chronic conditions not accounted for in simple screening questionnaires.
limitations.lim4Desc: Any persistent or severe symptoms (such as chronic exhaustion, chest discomfort, severe dizziness, or neurological numbness) warrant immediate in-person evaluation by a qualified medical doctor or registered dietitian.

rdaRoles.vitamin_b12: Nerve sheath integrity, RBC maturation, DNA synthesis
rdaRoles.vitamin_d: Intestinal calcium uptake, bone mineralization, immunity
rdaRoles.calcium: Bone density, neuromuscular transmission, muscle contraction
rdaRoles.vitamin_a: Rhodopsin dark adaptation, mucosal epithelial barrier defense
rdaRoles.folate: Cell division, rapid tissue growth, neural tube protection
rdaRoles.protein: Muscle mass maintenance, enzyme & antibody synthesis

about.title: About NutriSense: Objectives & Methodology
about.subtitle: An evidence-informed platform designed to evaluate nutritional risk patterns and raise public dietary awareness through transparent, rule-based analysis.
about.problemDesc: Micronutrient deficiencies (often termed 'hidden hunger') affect a substantial proportion of the global population, particularly across diverse Indian dietary settings. Low intake of bioavailable iron, Vitamin B12 in strict vegetarian diets, minimal sunlight-derived Vitamin D in urban lifestyles, and inadequate dietary diversity often go unnoticed until clinical symptoms become severe.
about.solutionDesc: NutriSense provides an accessible, evidence-backed self-assessment tool that bridges the gap between daily food habits and clinical nutrition benchmarks (such as ICMR-NIN 2024 and WHO guidelines). It analyzes self-reported food group frequencies and lifestyle factors to generate transparent, explainable preliminary risk indications with whole-food dietary adjustments.
about.techSubtitle: Engineered entirely client-side with Next.js and TypeScript for privacy, speed, and reliability.

techCards.nextjsDesc: App Router architecture providing fast client-side routing, server-rendered static guidelines, and accessible UI components.
techCards.tsDesc: Strict type safety across assessment data structures and clean, responsive health-tech design system with curated accessible contrast.
techCards.rechartsDesc: Interactive multi-axis radar charts and progress distributions illustrating nutrient adequacy vs risk vulnerability.
techCards.ruleDesc: Deterministic, explainable rule engine that cross-references dietary intakes, antinutrient inhibitors (tannins/phytates), and biological sex.
techCards.zeroBackendDesc: No Spring Boot, Java backend, MySQL, Firebase, or cloud database tracking. Safe from cloud data leaks and external API downtime.
techCards.storageDesc: Assessment responses and evaluation summaries survive page reloads securely within the user's own local browser storage.

about.methodologySubtitle: Every score and risk level generated by NutriSense is deterministic and directly traceable back to specific user answers.

methodologyPoints.point1Desc: Food group frequencies are weighted based on their nutrient density and biological availability. For example, plant-based iron is scored alongside Vitamin C consumption (which triples non-heme absorption) and mealtime tea/coffee habits (which inhibit uptake).
methodologyPoints.point2Desc: Reported cues (fatigue, pale appearance, cramps, skin changes) are treated as secondary weighting multipliers that elevate risk when dietary intake is suboptimal.
methodologyPoints.point3Desc: Results are stratified into 'Low Risk Indication' (< 35 score), 'Moderate Risk Indication' (35–59 score), and 'Elevated Risk Indication' (≥ 60 score), accompanied by transparent explanations and ICMR food sources.
